background: Darlington Building Society is a small regional mutual in the north-east of England, funded by retail savings from its branches and lending on residential mortgages, including self-build and later-life lending.
synthesis: None of the three main agencies rates the society, so the case rests on its own figures. Capital is mixed, with CET1 of 14.4% below the UK building society median and leverage of 5.9% just above it; liquidity is uneven, LCR of 172% in the bottom quarter but NSFR of 183% in the top quarter. Since 31 Dec 2022 CET1 has fallen 1.1 points, leverage 0.6 points and LCR 51 points, while NSFR has risen 7 points, and the figures run only to 31 Dec 2025.
